results.trace: Ran `pnpm vitest run --config vitest.config.ts tests/verify/R1-1.test.ts` (happy-dom). The test creates the race UI, resets it, syncs countdown 3 (.ui-hud has is-entering), pauses, then reset() again and syncs countdown 3, which is the pause → RESTART RACE path (game.ts:106 restart → startRace → ui.reset at :277; setPaused allows a pause in the countdown, :165). A MutationObserver watches the class attribute on .ui-hud and .ui-touch. It fails: 'HUD entry restarted: expected 0 to be greater than 0'. race-ui.ts:107 `if (on === entering) return` makes enter(true) a no-op, because entering is only cleared at GO (:198-199). The class never changes, so the CSS slide doesn't restart.
results.reason: A reset during the countdown never touches the entry classes, so the restarted race gets no slide-in. That breaks the spec's 'A race reset slides HUD panels and touch slots in'.

results.trace: Ran `pnpm vitest run --config vitest.config.ts tests/verify/R2-1.test.ts` (happy-dom). The test stubs each slot's getBoundingClientRect with a +195px offset (the mid-slide translateY(50vh) at 390px, touch-controls.css:139-157 with backwards fill), then reset() and a countdown sync. zones() gives GAS cy=520 and caches it (touch-controls.ts:129 `cache ??= measure()`). Then the offset goes to 0, animationend fires on the slots and countdown 2 is synced. zones() still returns cy 520: 'expected 520 to be 325'. Only resize, wake() and enter() invalidate, and enter(false) runs only at GO. src/input/touch.ts:85 onMove ignores pointers that aren't held, so a finger resting on GAS through GO is never picked up.
results.reason: Zones cached mid-slide stay stale until GO, so presses on the controls where they are drawn miss during the countdown.

results.trace: Same mechanism as R1-1 (race-ui.ts:107 guard, reset during the countdown).

Compared tests/ui/hud-motion.ts:69-77 with harness/screens/browser.ts:123-138. renderStage also calls __settle() (it finishes animations or pauses them at 0) and waits for fonts. stage() deliberately sets reducedMotion before rendering and leaves animations unsettled.
results.reason: The two helpers do different jobs (settle vs no settle, media emulated before render). This is a four-line test-plumbing overlap, and changing it could alter what the AC tests observe. That is a style preference, not a defect.

results.trace: src/ui/hud.ts:104 `let entering = false;` and :196-200 `enter(on) { if (on === entering) return; entering = on; element.classList.toggle('is-entering', on); }`. src/ui/race-ui.ts:93 `let entering = false;` and :106-111 `function enter(on) { if (on === entering) return; entering = on; hud.enter(on); touch.enter(on); }`. A grep for `\.enter(` in src finds only race-ui.ts:109-110. So hud's flag mirrors race-ui's exactly, and its guard can never fire. touch-controls.ts:134-138 enter() has no such flag. The extra guard also blocks the R1-1 restart.
results.reason: Duplicated state and guard: the HUD's own entering flag does the same job as race-ui's flag, which already guards its only caller.

results.trace: Same stale zones() cache during the entry slide (touch-controls.ts:129, 134-138).
Same race-ui.ts enter() guard during a reset in the countdown.

src/ui/hud.css:240 `.ui-hud-pos.is-bump { animation: ui-hud-bump var(--duration-stamp) var(--ease-stamp); }` and :282-286 `@keyframes ui-hud-bump { 50% { transform: scale(var(--ui-hud-bump)); } }` (1.12). The 0% and 100% keyframes are implicit (scale 1). A CSS timing function applies per keyframe interval, so the stamp curve cubic-bezier(.3,1.5,.5,1) (tokens.css:110) runs on 0→50% and again on 50→100%. Its output peaks at y(0.6)=3·0.16·0.6·1.5+3·0.4·0.36+0.216=1.08. Segment 1: 1+0.12·1.08≈1.13 (overshoot up). Segment 2: 1.12−0.12·1.08≈0.99, which dips below rest. UI_RULES.md:69 says 'stamp … one overshoot, landings only' and board 05 says 'one overshoot at most'.
results.reason: The bump overshoots twice and the second dips the panel below its rest size, which breaks the one-overshoot and landings-only stamp rule.

results.trace: src/ui/race-ui.ts:96-100 eventMotion uses `since < EVENT_TICKS`. src/ui/stages/hud-motion.stage.ts syncs events only at since=0 (overtake 1200→1201, new-lap 2421→2422) and since=10 ('-done' at 1211/2432). grep finds EVENT_TICKS and is-bump/is-stamp in no other test. With EVENT_TICKS=1, AC1/AC3/AC7 still see the class at since 0 and AC4 sees none at 10, so every test passes. In the game, sync runs every frame, so hud.events(null…) would strip the class at the next tick and cut the 160ms move after about 16ms.
results.reason: Nothing tests that the motion classes stay on for the whole move. A shortened window survives every test, while the game syncs every frame.

results.trace: src/ui/race-ui.ts:140 `synced = false;` in reset(). Every hud-motion stage builds a fresh createRaceUi through raceStage() (stage.ts:101-115), so `let synced = false` (race-ui.ts:92) already holds and no test resets the same UI twice while checking event classes (race-ui.test.ts checks only the countdown roundel). game.ts creates one ui and calls ui.reset() per race (:277). Without line 140, race 2's first sync at P4 differs from the reset state.position=1 (:123), so posEvents/posTick are set and Pos bumps during the countdown, breaking AC2's 'first sync is not an event' for every race after the first. No test fails.
results.reason: Resetting the baseline across races, the path the real game uses, has no test. Deleting it survives every test.

results.trace: src/ui/hud.ts:46-54 motion() toggles `is-again` on `n % 2 === 1`, and hud.css:243/249/256 swap the keyframe names. No stage syncs a second position or lap change within 10 ticks (hud-motion.stage.ts), and AC1 only asserts animation-name is non-null. With the is-again toggle deleted, all tests pass, but a second overtake inside the window keeps the same animation-name, so CSS doesn't restart the bump. The plan audit explicitly required this restart.
results.reason: The restart path the plan audit asked for has no test, and removing it leaves every test passing.

results.trace: hud.css @keyframes ui-hud-enter `from { transform: translateY(-50vh) }` and touch-controls.css:154-157 ui-touch-enter `from { transform: translateY(50vh) }`. tests/ui/hud-motion.ts probe() reads only animationName, animationDuration, animationTimingFunction and animationDelay, never keyframes or transforms. Flipping either sign keeps AC5 passing. The plan audit noted that 'AC5 doesn't check the direction' and asked for down/up slides.
results.reason: The slide direction the plan audit called out (top panels down, controls up) has no test, so reversing it passes every test.
